tips.title: Check that the foreign school or programme is recognised before you pay tuition
tips.cost: No cost to check the regulator's list. A credential evaluation may have a fee.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no single 'approved school' list for every country. Check the institution's recognition with its national regulator, the Indian embassy or consulate, and the UGC or the AIU if you want the degree recognised in India. A scholarship or a visa may depend on the institution's recognition. Do not pay an agent for a 'guaranteed' admission or a 'recognised' degree.
tips.benefit: The UGC and the Association of Indian Universities publish the recognition and equivalence rules for a foreign degree. The destination's education ministry or regulator lists the accredited institutions. The Indian mission can confirm whether a college is genuine. A student visa usually requires an admission letter from a recognised institution. A fake university can leave you with a degree that no employer or university accepts.
tips.sources: University Grants Commission. <https://www.ugc.gov.in/>; Association of Indian Universities. <https://www.aiu.ac.in/>; Ministry of External Affairs. <https://www.mea.gov.in/>; Ministry of Education. <https://www.education.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A 'pathway' college that is not accredited may not lead to a degree. Check the course, the campus and the recognition separately. Do not pay the full tuition before the admission letter is verified.

tips.title: A U.S. court has put the fixed-stay rule for F-1 students on hold: 'duration of status' still applies for now
tips.cost: No cost. Note the programme end date from your I-20 and set a reminder about 90 days ahead. The I-20 is the form your school issues to certify your eligibility for F-1 status. Check the international student office page once a semester rather than relying on social media.
tips.inPlainWords: The U.S. proposed to replace 'stay until you finish your course' with a fixed maximum stay of four years and a 30-day window to leave afterwards. A federal court stayed the rule one day before it was to take effect, so the older rules still apply while the case continues: you may stay for the length of your programme, and you get 60 days after you finish to leave or change status. A stay is not a repeal. The government can appeal, and the rule could come back in amended form. Write the programme end date on your I-20 into your calendar, and check your university's international student office page each term.
tips.benefit: The rule was announced in July 2026 with an effective date of 15 September 2026. It would have ended 'duration of status' for F, J and I visa holders and substituted a fixed four-year admission with an extension application. On 14 September 2026 a U.S. District Court in Massachusetts stayed it nationwide under section 705 of the Administrative Procedure Act; the court did not vacate the rule, and the government can appeal. While the stay stands, F-1 students keep the current position: admission for the duration of status, and a 60-day grace period after the programme ends.
tips.sources: U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts. Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security, No. 1:26-cv-13799-FDS (order of 14 September 2026). <https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/74661796/presidents-alliance-on-higher-education-and-immigration-v-united-states/>; 8 CFR 214.2(f), students and exchange visitors. <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-214/section-214.2>; U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. <https://www.uscis.gov/>
tips.caveats: This is a court stay, not a final decision, and the position can change at short notice. If the rule is revived, an extension would have to be filed before your authorised stay expires; there is no automatic renewal. The proposal also covered J visas, with different details, so check the rule for your own visa category. Students planning a multi-year programme, a transfer or a post-study work period should not assume the current position will last. Ask the international student office before you travel or change course.

tips.title: The maximum allowed work hours are strict limits in the U.S., Canada, UK, and Australia — exceeding them violates visa terms.
tips.cost: There’s no cost involved. You simply need to track your weekly hours yourself. The difficulty lies in employers often claiming “no one checks extra hours,” but you must never believe this.
tips.inPlainWords: All four countries set clear caps on how many hours international students may work. Going over these limits breaches visa conditions, potentially leading to visa revocation, deportation, or extra scrutiny during future applications. The limits are: 20 hours per week in the U.S., 20 hours weekly for degree students and 10 hours for non-degree students in the UK, 24 hours per week in Canada, and 48 hours every two weeks in Australia. Hours worked at multiple jobs must be combined.
tips.benefit: F-1 students in the U.S. may work up to 20 hours per week on campus during term time, with the same 20-hour weekly cap applying to approved off-campus jobs; full-time work is allowed during holidays. This is stipulated under 8 CFR 214.2(f)(9) of U.S. federal immigration regulations. UK students pursuing degree-level courses may work 20 hours weekly during term time, while those on non-degree programs are limited to 10 hours per week; no work is permitted for part-time students at all. Self-employment is also prohibited, meaning you cannot work for yourself, nor may you serve as a professional athlete or performer. These rules are outlined in the UK immigration rules for students, specifically Student ST26.1 and ST26.5. Eligible full-time students in Canada may work up to 24 hours per week off campus, per Article 186(v) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR). For Australian student visas, the limit is 48 hours every two weeks while classes are in session; this restriction does not apply to research-based master’s or PhD students, nor their dependents.
tips.sources: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(9). <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-214/section-214.2>; UK Home Office. Immigration Rules Appendix Student (ST26.1, ST26.5). <https://www.gov.uk/guidance/immigration-rules/immigration-rules-appendix-student>; IRCC. Work off campus as an international student. <https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-off-campus.html>; Australian Government Department of Home Affairs. Student visa (subclass 500). <https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500>
tips.caveats: In the U.S., any off-campus work must first receive official approval; you cannot begin working while your I-765 work permit application is still pending. Older Canadian work permits may list a 20-hour weekly cap, but if you still meet all eligibility criteria, current regulations permit up to 24 hours per week. The UK’s self-employment ban is broadly interpreted: taking private contracts, running an online store, or working as a freelancer all count as prohibited self-employment.

tips.title: The core requirement for eligibility is “full-time enrollment”: any gap due to suspension, withdrawal, or transfer disqualifies you from working.
tips.cost: No cost involved. Before suspending, withdrawing, or transferring schools, contact your school’s international student office to confirm your current status.
tips.inPlainWords: Whether you can work depends on whether you are currently enrolled full-time. Once you are suspended, withdrawn, expelled, or not attending classes during a transfer, your right to work ends immediately. Continuing to work in such cases constitutes illegal employment. Many assume that as long as their visa remains valid, they are still eligible, but in reality their status has already been revoked.
tips.benefit: Canadian regulations explicitly prohibit off-campus work during approved suspension periods, as well as for students who are not actively enrolled during a transfer. Work privileges can only be reinstated after resuming full-time studies. In the U.S., off-campus work eligibility is granted only to F-1 students whose SEVIS record shows an “Active” status — this system tracks valid enrollment for international students, and such students must also maintain full-time coursework. In the UK, work permits are issued based on course type; students on part-time programs are not permitted to work.
tips.sources: IRCC. Work off campus as an international student. <https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-off-campus.html>; U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Study in the States. Working in the United States. <https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/work/working-in-the-united-states>; UK Home Office. Immigration Rules Appendix Student (ST26.1). <https://www.gov.uk/guidance/immigration-rules/immigration-rules-appendix-student>
tips.caveats: If you are feeling overwhelmed by coursework and considering reducing your course load, first verify exactly how many credits constitute full-time enrollment — falling below that threshold will disqualify you from work eligibility, often even before any work permit issues arise. Students who are expelled or whose programs are terminated typically lose their eligibility status on the same day; do not wait for an official notice from the school before taking action.

tips.title: United States: You must report your new address within 10 days of moving
tips.cost: No cost at all. Submitting the address change online takes just ten minutes.
tips.inPlainWords: If you move within the United States, the law requires you to inform USCIS within ten days. Failing to do so is no minor issue. First, it is illegal; second, any mail sent to you by USCIS could easily be lost.
tips.benefit: Under 8 CFR 265.1, foreign nationals required by law to register must report any change of address to USCIS within ten days of moving. Reporting via the official USCIS channels lets you both confirm the address change and provide your new address.
tips.sources: 8 CFR 265.1. <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-265/section-265.1>; USCIS. AR-11, Alien's Change of Address Card. <https://www.uscis.gov/ar-11>
tips.caveats: Reporting to USCIS is separate from updating your school records. You must also update your SEVIS record through your educational institution, which maintains your student visa status. The other three countries also mandate reporting address changes to immigration authorities or schools, though both the deadlines and procedures differ by country. Always follow the instructions posted on your local immigration authority’s website.

tips.title: Read the MEA's travel advisory for your destination and the Indian mission's student notices before you go
tips.cost: Free. Read it once before you commit to a course and once each semester; a two-minute check is cheaper than a ruined year.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not publish a country-by-country list of 'unsafe' study destinations. What the government does publish is the Ministry of External Affairs' travel advisories, and each Indian embassy or consulate posts local security, visa and consular notices, often including ones for students. Read the advisory for your destination before you pay a deposit, and check the mission's page once a term. An advisory is the government's written assessment of conditions there: if it says to avoid non-essential travel, treat that as a real signal rather than as paperwork.
tips.benefit: The Ministry of External Affairs lists current travel advisories by country, and the list of Indian missions and posts links to the embassy or consulate that covers your city. A mission's page carries local notices, consular contact details and, in a crisis, instructions for Indian nationals. Together with the destination government's own travel advice and your institution's international office, these are the written sources you can point to when a family member or an employer asks whether a place is safe. A mission can also tell you which local lawyer or doctor to approach after an accident or a crime.
tips.sources: Ministry of External Affairs, travel advisories. <https://www.mea.gov.in/travel-advisories.htm>; Ministry of External Affairs, Indian missions and posts abroad. <https://www.mea.gov.in/indian-mission-abroad.htm>; Ministry of External Affairs. <https://www.mea.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Advisories change without notice and this page cannot stay current, so read the MEA page itself. An advisory is not a ban: it does not decide your visa, and a university may still admit you. It can matter for insurance and for a scholarship, so keep a printout with your documents. The mission cannot get your agent's fee back or overrule a foreign court. Save the mission's address and emergency number in your phone before you fly.

tips.title: Australia: OSHC must cover the entire stay without any gaps; lack of proof may lead to denied entry
tips.cost: Several thousand to tens of thousands of rupees. Purchase it once based on the length of your visa; if you’re studying for several years, buy coverage for that entire period.
tips.inPlainWords: Australia makes overseas student health insurance (OSHC) a mandatory visa requirement — it’s not optional. The policy must cover your entire stay in the country. When renewing or switching policies, there must be no lapse in coverage. If you cannot produce proof of insurance upon arrival, you may be denied entry on the spot. Family members accompanying you as dependents must each purchase their own policy.
tips.benefit: According to Australian Department of Home Affairs regulations, student visa applicants and their dependents must obtain OSHC, which must remain in effect throughout their entire stay in Australia without any interruptions. The policy must be issued by an insurer approved by Australian authorities, except for applicants who qualify for exemptions. There must be no gap between the end date of one policy and the start date of a new one. Failure to provide proof of active coverage upon entry can result in denial of entry. For travelers arriving in Australia prior to their course start date, the policy start date must be set to the actual date of arrival.
tips.sources: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs. Student visa (subclass 500). <https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500>
tips.caveats: If your school arranges the insurance for you, be sure to confirm the insurer’s name, the policy’s start and end dates, and the policy number — these details must be included in your visa application. Purchasing coverage for a shorter period than needed can cause issues when you apply to renew your visa; it’s better to buy coverage that extends well beyond your graduation date.

tips.title: UK: Besides the visa fee, there is an annual healthcare surcharge — £776 per year for students, paid in full at application time
tips.cost: The visa fee is £558. There is also a healthcare surcharge of £776 per year, both of which must be paid in full at the time of application.
tips.inPlainWords: The amount you pay to go to the UK isn’t limited to just the visa fee. You also have to prepay the healthcare surcharge based on the length of your visa, which is required to access the UK’s National Health Service. For a two‑year visa, that means paying £1,552 upfront. Add this to the visa fee, and you’ll need to budget for this total amount before you travel.
tips.benefit: The fee for a UK student visa is £558, regardless of whether you apply from outside the UK or extend/change your visa status while already there. In addition, the healthcare surcharge must be paid to use the National Health Service; it is calculated per year of your visa and paid in full at application. For students and their dependents, the charge is £776 per year — so a two‑year visa requires a payment of £1,552. Other applicant categories pay £1,035 per year. If your visa lasts more than six months but less than a full year, the charge is still applied for a full year.
tips.sources: UK Government. Student visa. <https://www.gov.uk/student-visa>; UK Government. Pay for UK healthcare as part of your immigration application. <https://www.gov.uk/healthcare-immigration-application>
tips.caveats: Both the fee amounts and exchange rates may change; always refer to the two pages listed under Sources for the most current figures. Generally, students aged 18 or older enrolled in degree programmes can stay for up to five years, while those on non‑degree courses are limited to two years. Use these timeframes to estimate the total healthcare surcharge you’ll need to pay.

tips.title: Allow time for degree equivalence and document attestation before you return to India
tips.cost: The AIU fee is modest; an agent's fee is avoidable. Attestation has a fee.
tips.inPlainWords: A foreign degree may need an equivalence certificate from the Association of Indian Universities for a government job or a higher degree, and the documents may need an apostille or a consular attestation. Start before you leave: collect the transcript, the degree certificate and the marksheets, and check the AIU's current rules. A private agent cannot make an unrecognised degree recognised.
tips.benefit: The Association of Indian Universities issues an equivalence certificate for a foreign degree, and the Ministry of External Affairs attests documents for use abroad or in India. The Hague Apostille Convention applies to some countries. A government employer or a university may ask for the equivalence and the attestation. The process takes weeks, so plan ahead.
tips.sources: Association of Indian Universities. <https://www.aiu.ac.in/>; Ministry of External Affairs, attestation. <https://www.mea.gov.in/>; University Grants Commission. <https://www.ugc.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A degree from an unrecognised institution may not get equivalence. Check the AIU list and the course duration. Keep the original documents; a photocopy is not enough.

tips.title: Before you enrol, check how the degree will be recognised in India: AIU equivalence, MEA attestation and the professional council
tips.cost: AIU equivalence and MEA attestation both charge a fee, and both take weeks rather than days. An agent's 'guaranteed equivalence' or 'fast-track certification' fee buys nothing that you cannot do yourself.
tips.inPlainWords: There is no Indian list that flags particular foreign universities. What decides your future is whether the degree will be accepted here: the Association of Indian Universities issues an equivalence certificate for a foreign degree, the Ministry of External Affairs apostilles or attests your documents, and for a professional course the relevant council decides recognition. A programme sold as 'no language test, no need to travel, master's in a few months' is exactly the kind that fails that check. Verify before you pay, not after.
tips.benefit: AIU equivalence is what a government employer, a public university or a higher degree usually asks for. MEA attestation or an apostille is what makes an Indian document usable abroad, and a foreign document usable here. For a professional course the council that regulates the profession also has a say: the National Medical Commission for medicine, the dental council for dentistry, the Bar Council of India for law, and the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India for accountancy. The UGC's rules on foreign degrees and on online and distance programmes decide whether a course delivered mostly online counts at all. None of these steps can be skipped by an agent.
tips.sources: Association of Indian Universities, equivalence of degrees. <https://aiu.ac.in/frontpage/equivalence-of-degree/>; Association of Indian Universities, equivalence committee. <https://aiu.ac.in/governance/equivalence-commitee/>; Ministry of External Affairs. <https://www.mea.gov.in/>; University Grants Commission. <https://www.ugc.gov.in/>; National Medical Commission. <https://www.nmc.org.in/>; Bar Council of India. <https://www.bci.org.in/>; Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. <https://www.icai.org/>
tips.caveats: Equivalence is decided case by case, on the syllabus, the duration, the mode of study and the institution's recognition in its own country, so a name that sounds familiar is not enough. A professional council's recognition is a separate question from AIU equivalence: clearing one does not give you the other. A degree awarded for a course delivered online, or by an institution that is not recognised where it operates, may get no equivalence at all, and no payment can change that. Anyone offering to certify a degree through an 'internal channel' is running a fraud.

tips.title: United States: When working under post-completion OPT, track your days of unemployment; cumulative unemployment cannot exceed 90 days (150 days total for STEM extensions)
tips.cost: Free. Keep a meticulous personal log recording start and end dates of every period of unemployment. Promptly report new employer details and employment start dates to your university's Designated School Official (DSO) through the SEVP portal. The friction is the stress of watching the 90-day clock tick during difficult job markets.
tips.inPlainWords: Optional Practical Training (OPT) grants F-1 international students temporary employment authorization in the United States, but legal immigration status during OPT strictly depends on active employment. If cumulative days of unemployment exceed 90 days, your F-1 SEVIS status may be terminated, requiring you to leave the United States. If granted a 24-month STEM OPT extension, the aggregate cumulative unemployment limit across the entire period (initial OPT plus STEM extension) cannot exceed 150 days. Having an unrecorded employer in SEVIS counts as unemployment.
tips.benefit: Under U.S. federal immigration regulations (8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E) and 8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(i)(B)), maintaining F-1 non-immigrant status during post-completion OPT requires active qualifying employment. A student may not accrue more than a cumulative total of 90 days of unemployment during the initial 12-month post-completion OPT authorization period. Students granted a 24-month STEM OPT extension receive an additional 60 days of allowed unemployment, resulting in a maximum aggregate cap of 150 days across the entire OPT lifecycle. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) guidance decrees that if no employer information is reported in the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS), the student is classified as unemployed. Once 90 days of accrued unemployment are reached, SEVP officers possess regulatory authority to manually terminate the SEVIS record. U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) rules dictate that initial post-completion OPT applications can be filed up to 90 days prior to academic program completion and no later than 60 days post-completion, and must be submitted to USCIS within 30 days of the DSO issuing the OPT recommendation in SEVIS.
tips.sources: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E), (f)(11)(i)(B). <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-214/section-214.2>; U.S. ICE SEVP, SEVIS Help Hub. F-1 Optional Practical Training (OPT). <https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/sevis-help-hub/student-records/fm-student-employment/f-1-optional-practical-training-opt>; USCIS. Optional Practical Training (OPT) for F-1 Students. <https://www.uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/students-and-exchange-visitors/optional-practical-training-opt-for-f-1-students>; DHS (2026). Optional Practical Training Fees (Proposed Rule, October 8, 2026). <https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/08/2026-20660/optional-practical-training-fees>
tips.caveats: Regulatory rules are actively evolving. Two developments require close monitoring: First, litigation surrounding DHS regulations has created uncertainties regarding application filing windows, making it safest to submit your Form I-765 before graduation rather than relying on grace periods. Second, DHS published a proposed rulemaking on October 8, 2026 considering user fees for OPT adjudications ($70,000 for initial OPT and $30,000 for subsequent filings under regulatory consideration); always verify effective rulemaking status before submitting applications.

tips.title: Canada: Obtain a Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL/TAL) through your designated learning institution before submitting a study permit application; public master's and doctoral students are exempt from 2026
tips.cost: Free from the government; requested through your admitting educational institution. Most designated learning institutions (DLIs) require accepting an offer and paying a tuition deposit before applying for a PAL.
tips.inPlainWords: For international students heading to Canada, most post-secondary study permit applications require submitting a Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) or Territorial Attestation Letter (TAL), which serves as evidence that the applicant falls under the provincial study permit allocation cap. This document must accompany the initial visa submission and cannot be retroactively submitted. If your visa is approved, refused, or if you transfer institutions, a new PAL is required. Graduate students pursuing master's or doctoral degrees at public institutions are exempt starting in 2026.
tips.benefit: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) mandates that international study permit applicants submit an official Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) or Territorial Attestation Letter (TAL) issued by the province or territory where the designated learning institution is located, confirming the applicant has been allocated a permit within the annual national cap. Applications submitted without a PAL/TAL are returned without processing. Primary and secondary school students (kindergarten to grade 12) are exempt. Effective January 1, 2026, students admitted to master's and doctoral degree programs at public universities are also exempt. Students bound for Quebec submit the Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ). Non-paying exchange students and students renewing permits within the same institution/level are also exempt. PALs typically remain valid until the end of the calendar year of issuance (December 31). If an initial permit application is refused, reapplying requires requesting a newly issued PAL. Starting January 22, 2025, transferring between designated learning institutions also requires securing a new PAL.
tips.sources: IRCC. Provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter (updated Sept 2, 2026). <https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/provincial-attestation-letter.html>; IRCC. Study permit: Get the right documents (updated Oct 6, 2026). <https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents.html>
tips.caveats: Study permit cap allocations are reset annually. Always review the latest IRCC documentation guidelines prior to submission. Before paying non-refundable tuition deposits to obtain a PAL, clarify the institution's refund policies in the event of permit refusal. For off-campus work hour limits in Canada, see Chapter 32, Rule 3.
